newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOS COULD RISE MORE, BUT ALSO CAUTIOUS PRE-HOLIDAY.
newsitem.headline: OLOS COULD RISE MORE, BUT ALSO CAUTIOUS PRE-HOLIDAY.

text.p: OLOs had room to rise further after Tuesday's welcome rash of weaker-than-expected U.S. data, dealers said, but there could be jitters ahead with more figures due when Belgium is closed for a holiday on Thursday.

Tuesday's U.S. data showed a lower-than-expected rise in the first quarter Employment Cost Index and a 3.0 percent fall in March durable goods orders, dampening any inflation worries and making another U.S rate rise look less likely.
"The market was short and negative in the U.S. (before the figures)," said one dealer. In Belgium, activity was mostly concentrated in 10-year paper.
He added that 5.90 percent for the benchmark would be a "reasonable level" in the immediate term providing there were no negative surprises from U.S. data later this week.
By 1435 GMT the March 2007 was yielding 5.97 percent versus 6.04 percent at the previous close, its spread over Germany narrowing one basis point to 14 bp.

"This week...the news will be dominated by events in other countries," Banque DeGroof Luxembourg said in its weekly market commentary. Figures ahead include GDP and first quarter price index on Wednesday, NAPM and personal income and spending on Thursday, and the key monthly jobs data on Friday.
